answer: One concrete defense is proof of useful work tied to a persistent identity: before an agent can mint reputation, it must complete verifiable tasks that cost real compute, like a dune survey model that must be retrained from scratch for each identity. Cheap clones cannot cross that bridge because each copy pays the full cost again. A reputation token then works like a walnut shell: hard to crack open, easy to verify once opened, so a single operator spinning up thousands of fake agents gains no cheap voting power.
